why: The array rows of the library table as heap transitions in the proof lane. flip returning the receiver through a local bound after the reverse: proved. dropFirstCopy and count untouched: proved. head slices three for two and joined concatenates in the other order: unproved, witnessed. dropFirst (a shift for a splice(0, 1)) and dropTwo (two splice(0, 1) for one splice(0, 2)) leave the same reachable graph but not the same heap: splice allocates the removed part, which nobody keeps; the whole-heap lemma fails and the canonical-heap certificate (equal up to a renaming of fresh cells and up to dropped allocations) proves both. head and joined fail the canonical reading too: the named fresh cells differ.
